title_as_printed: Experimental values of oxygen solubility (umol kg-1), for temperatures from 8 to 35 C and salinity values from 37.77 permil to 133.15 permil
pressure_note: 'oxygen solubility C* (umol kg-1) at 1 atm of pressure'; samples equilibrated by bubbling atmospheric air, total atmospheric pressure recorded with a Fortin barometer; the paper does not state whether the 1 atm is total or O2 partial pressure and whether values were corrected for water vapour or to standard pressure
gas_basis_note: gas is O2 from air; no gas mole fractions reported
volume_basis_evidence: unit is umol per kg ('umol kg-1'); the paper does not state kg of solution or kg of water (Weiss-type seawater convention suggests kg of solution)

value.what: oxygen solubility in evaporated seawater from air-saturation (Winkler titration); kg basis is solution (seawater convention, 'C* is the solubility in umol kg-1 in air-saturated seawater at one atmosphere of pressure', compared with Benson and Krause 1984); inferred, not literally stated

composition.other_species: evaporated natural seawater from the Bay of Cadiz (Spain), diluted with distilled/natural samples; ionic composition not quantified; salinity measured with induction salinometer calibrated with KCl solutions, printed with the permil sign

conversion_needs: salinity (permil, evaporated seawater) is not a molality; needs a seawater-composition assumption
notes: Printed as a wide table (T rows x 11 salinity columns, rotated page); stacked here into 11 blocks of 28 temperatures (35 down to 8 C, order as printed), one label row per salinity. Samples above 37.77 permil are natural evaporated seawater; 0 to 37.77 permil are dilutions. Values are 'mean' solubilities of at least three measurements per T. Series are visibly noisy in places (e.g. S=6.05 at 35 to 32 C and S=13.08 vs 6.05 at 35 C: 213.7 vs 194.1; S=19.23 at 11-8 C above S=13.08) -- reported as printed, not corrected.
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: kg basis inferred as kg of SOLUTION from the paper's comparison with the seawater convention of Weiss/Benson and Krause (agreement within 6 uM); the builder must convert to kg water (m_water = m_solution/(1 - S/1000)). The ionic composition of the evaporated Bay of Cadiz seawater is never quantified (salinity by induction salinometer calibrated with KCl), so the reference-seawater ion assumption is unreliable at S >= about 97 permil; the practical salinity scale is not defined above 42. Irregular entries in the S=6.05 and S=13.08 columns at 31-35 C are authentic print. Values are air-saturated (C*), so they are stored as the binary O2-water equivalent with O2 at 0.20946 of (P - psat), like the Millero 2002 oxygen tables.

air_equilibrated.evidence: the paper compares its values with Benson and Krause (1984) and defines C* as the solubility in air-saturated seawater at one atmosphere of pressure, i.e. O2 at 0.2095 of the air; found by the inter-source consensus check (values 0.2 x the pure-O2 solubilities of Fox 1909 and Cosgrove 1981), 2026-10-03
